newsitem.title: USA: Ford posts record Q2 profits of $2.53 billion.
newsitem.headline: Ford posts record Q2 profits of $2.53 billion.

text.p: Ford Motor Co. said Wednesday its second quarter profit jumped 33 percent to $2.53 billion, an all-time quarterly record.
The U.S. No. 2 automaker credited its performance to reduced automotive operating costs and the introduction of several new, redesigned cars and trucks.

Ford earned $2.06 on a per-share basis, beating the First Call Corp. analyst consensus estimate of $1.82. Included in the results was a gain of $100 million, reflecting a gain from the initial public offering of Hertz Corp., and a charge for closing several plants and the sale of Ford's heavy truck business to Freightliner.
A year ago, Ford posted profits of $1.90 billion, or $1.56 a share.

Net income from Ford's worldwide automotive operations rose to $1.74 billion from $1.10 billion. The increase reflected strong profits in Ford's core U.S. automotive operations, which nearly doubled to $1.19 billion from $697 million. Worldwide sales and revenues at Ford were $40.3 billion compared to $39 billion.

"We're pleased to see automotive earnings continuing to improve," Ford Chairman Alex Trotman said in a statement. But he warned that more actions are needed in Europe before the automaker will be able to achieve its long-term objectives.
